### 03.02 Synthetic coordinate-test images
The sinusoidal sampling displacement has amplitude 15 px and returns to zero at both horizontal ends. The inverse uses a known map; this is not an estimated nonrigid method.

### 03.04 Projective mapping and curvature limitation
Projective corner agreement and pixel interpolation error are separate. The sinusoidal document has zero boundary displacement at left/right ends, so a boundary-fitted planar homography cannot recover its internal curvature. Known inverse deformation is an oracle, not an automatic method.

| curved line under identity corner homography | 11.12407 | y std px | DIAGNOSTIC |
| known inverse-map curved line | 0.0 | y std px | PASS |

### 11.02 Pilot research conclusions and gates
This is a reproducible diagnostic pilot with real pretrained inference and controlled classical variants. Any improvement beyond geometric sampling correctness requires confirmed benchmark alignment/metrics, not favorable-looking example images. The next production milestone is extraction of validated procedures into Python modules and full benchmark protocol reproduction.

| Classical contribution | Choose improved boundary handling or controlled nonrigid geometry only after examining pilot failure images. |
| UVDoc Final training loader | Do not report 2D grid L2 against pretrained outputs until random tight crop and coordinate transforms are consistently reproduced. |
